topic.title: Sanctuary cities
topic.proposition: Cities should limit their local police's cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.

messages.author: Participant A
messages.text: I understand why some people want local police fully aligned with federal immigration agents, but I think that approach undermines the basic promise that everyone in a community can turn to police without fear. When local officers act as an extension of federal immigration enforcement, it creates a patchwork of trust where someone's willingness to report a crime depends on their legal status. I also worry it sends a message that public safety takes a back seat to enforcement priorities set far away from the neighborhoods actually affected.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: I hear that concern about trust, but in my view the priority for local police has to include full cooperation with federal law, not selective enforcement based on local preference. When cities limit cooperation, it creates confusion about which laws actually apply depending on where you live, and it can mean people with serious violations simply aren't handed over when they should be. I think local governments don't have unlimited discretion to set aside federal enforcement priorities just because officials disagree with them, and consistency matters more than convenience.

messages.author: Participant A
messages.text: That's a fair point about consistency, and I don't dismiss it. But I think there's a difference between wholesale non-cooperation and simply declining to act as an extension of federal agents during routine encounters. When cities require police to prioritize community trust over information-sharing, it doesn't mean dangerous individuals go free, it means immigrant residents feel safe reporting crimes in the first place, and that strikes me as a real public safety benefit too, just distributed differently than you're describing.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: I take that concern seriously, and I agree there are real benefits to communities trusting police in everyday interactions. But most limits on cooperation I've seen go further than people assume, extending to withholding information even in cases involving serious criminal conduct, precisely because officials want to avoid federal involvement altogether. I think local governments shouldn't be able to draw those boundaries so broadly that federal law effectively becomes optional within city limits. This is the claim I am relying on.
